clue.text: Green, cleaner recycling involves tonnes

parts.note: a char, or charwoman, is a cleaner
T is the standard abbreviation for tonnes
recycling something is putting it to reuse

explanation.surface: An eco slogan: a cleaner, greener operation that recycles tonnes of waste.
explanation.definitionFit: Chartreuse is a yellowish-green colour, named after the liqueur.

clue.text: Encourage theatre leader to go and act

indicators.note: to go tells us a letter is dropped from the encouraging word

parts.note: to stimulate is to encourage

indicators.note: the leader of a word is its opening letter

explanation.surface: A director urging the head of the theatre company to get up and perform.
explanation.definitionFit: To simulate is to feign or pretend, i.e. to put on an act.

clue.text: Pop group with covers of Crosby provides role for elder brother

parts.note: ABBA, the Swedish pop group

indicators.note: the covers of a word are its outside letters

explanation.surface: A band covering Bing Crosby songs, with a part for an older sibling.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Elder brother' is not a sibling but a senior monk, an abbot; an abbacy is his office.
explanation.definitionFit: An abbacy is the office or position held by an abbot, a senior monastic brother.

clue.text: Onion or what it makes you do, if brought up

indicators.note: in a down clue, brought up means read from bottom to top

parts.note: an onion makes you cry, or blub

explanation.surface: An onion, or what it does to you if you eat it and it comes back up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Brought up' suggests vomiting, but in a down answer it turns the word around.
explanation.definitionFit: An onion is a bulb: the swollen underground storage organ of the plant.

clue.text: Wild tiger poked by entertainer with pen for another

indicators.note: poked by means the scrambled word has the next pieces pushed into it
wild signals the letters of tiger running loose in a new order

parts.note: a host entertains guests

explanation.surface: A circus scene: a wild tiger prodded by a ringmaster holding a pen.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Wild' makes GRITE, and 'poked by' pushes the other pieces in after its first letter; 'pen' here is a verb, to write.
explanation.definitionFit: To ghostwrite is to write a book or speech that is published under someone else's name.

clue.text: Toast's not fully three inches

indicators.note: not fully means the run of three words loses letters at both its ends

parts.note: three inches written out as INCH three times in a row

explanation.surface: A toast that is not even three inches of drink in the glass.
explanation.walkthrough: Write INCH three times and trim two letters from each end.
explanation.definitionFit: Chin-chin is an informal drinking toast, like cheers.

clue.text: Wood's in demand, we're told yew's discounted

indicators.note: discounted means the letter is left out of the word

parts.note: something in demand is popular

indicators.note: we're told means a word is spoken, giving its sound

parts.note: yew is said like the letter U

explanation.surface: A timber merchant reporting which woods are selling and that yew is on sale.
explanation.walkthrough: Yew is a wood too, which makes the surface plausible; here it only supplies the letter U.
explanation.definitionFit: Poplar is a tree and its timber, a type of wood.

clue.text: Seagull circles round, making beastly noise

indicators.note: circles means the bird word goes around the next piece

parts.note: a mew is a seagull
a round thing, O

explanation.surface: A seagull wheeling overhead, squawking.
explanation.definitionFit: A meow is a cat's cry, an animal's sound.

clue.text: Hard to improve image of means to treat shock

parts.note: H is the abbreviation for hard, as on pencils
to airbrush a photo is to touch it up flatteringly

explanation.surface: It's hard to touch up a picture of a remedy for trauma.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Shock' is not trauma but a shock of hair, a thick untidy mass.
explanation.definitionFit: A brush for the hair tames a thick mop, a shock of hair.

clue.text: Scientist's fine cutting tool for the garden

indicators.note: cutting means the next piece slices into the garden tool

parts.note: a hoe is a garden tool
OK means fine

explanation.surface: A scientist owns a decent garden tool for cutting.
explanation.walkthrough: Robert Hooke was a 17th-century English scientist, known for Hooke's law.
explanation.definitionFit: Robert Hooke was a famous English natural philosopher and experimenter.

clue.text: Loudly regret insult in actors' chatter

indicators.note: loudly means as spoken, giving the sound of the word

parts.note: to rue is to regret
a barb is a cutting insult

explanation.surface: Someone audibly regretting a slight thrown in the middle of actors' gossip.
explanation.definitionFit: Actors murmur the word rhubarb repeatedly to simulate background conversation.

clue.text: Brilliance from a star, having performed bass part?

parts.note: having performed a song, it has been sung
the bass part is the low one

explanation.surface: A star singer shining after performing the bass line.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Star' suggests a performer, but it is the sun.
explanation.definitionFit: Sunglow is the bright light or glow from the sun, the nearest star.

clue.text: Trot round a yard is quick

indicators.note: round means the Trot word goes around the next piece

parts.note: a Trot (Trotskyist) is a Red, a communist

explanation.surface: Jogging once around a yard is fast.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Trot' looks like jogging but is a Trotskyist, a left-winger.
explanation.definitionFit: Ready can mean prompt or quick, as in a ready answer or ready wit.

clue.text: US bookmaker may close in June

parts.note: may is another name for the hawthorn tree

indicators.note: the close of a word is its final letter

explanation.surface: An American betting firm might shut down in June.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bookmaker' is not a betting man but an author; Nathaniel Hawthorne wrote The Scarlet Letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Nathaniel Hawthorne was an American novelist, a maker of books.

clue.text: Racing venue in case more should run

parts.note: in and hip both mean fashionable
a pod is a seed case

indicators.note: should run means the letters of more run around into a new order

explanation.surface: At the racecourse, in case more horses run.
explanation.definitionFit: A hippodrome was an ancient Greek or Roman course for horse and chariot races.

clue.text: Hate helping to support boss

indicators.note: in a down clue, supporting means placed below the boss word

parts.note: an exec, an executive, is a boss
a ration is a helping or portion

explanation.surface: Hating to help prop up the boss.
explanation.definitionFit: Execration is utter loathing or the act of cursing someone.

clue.text: Saving boring marriage, a bishop's empty life is beyond reproach

indicators.note: boring means the saving word bores into the marriage word

parts.note: a marriage is a union
saving means except, as in all saving one
B is the abbreviation for bishop in chess notation

indicators.note: empty means only the outer letters remain

explanation.surface: A bishop leading a dull married life, surprisingly, is above criticism.
explanation.definitionFit: Something unexceptionable cannot be objected to, so it is faultless.

clue.text: I'm amazed, screening 2001 or one without a title

indicators.note: screening means the exclamation hides the next piece within it

parts.note: cor is an exclamation of surprise
2001 is two thousand (MM in Roman numerals) plus one

explanation.surface: Someone astonished at a showing of 2001: A Space Odyssey, or a film with no title.
explanation.definitionFit: A commoner is someone without a noble rank or title.

clue.text: Perhaps star in parliament holds a presentation

parts.note: best, as in star or top, for example

indicators.note: holds means the bird word holds the next piece inside it

parts.note: a parliament is the collective noun for owls, so an owl is one in it

explanation.surface: A star MP hosts an awards presentation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Parliament' is not Westminster but a group of owls.
explanation.definitionFit: A bestowal is the act of giving or conferring something, such as an award.

clue.text: Poet inflamed with mere kiss that's spontaneous

indicators.note: inflamed signals the letters heated and churned into a new order

explanation.surface: A poet, passion roused by a mere kiss, acts on impulse.
explanation.definitionFit: Extempore means done without preparation, improvised on the spot.

clue.text: Sensitive figure embarrassed when rejected

parts.note: ten is a number, a figure

indicators.note: rejected means turned back, so the word reads in reverse

parts.note: red-faced, embarrassed

explanation.surface: A sensitive person feeling embarrassed after being turned down.
explanation.definitionFit: Tender means sore or easily hurt, sensitive to the touch.

clue.text: Exchange rates that can be shocking

definitions.note: a description standing for a thing that delivers shocks

indicators.note: exchange means swap the letters around

explanation.surface: Currency exchange rates that can cause a nasty surprise.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Exchange rates' reads as one financial phrase, but 'Exchange' is the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: A Taser is a stun gun that delivers an electric jolt.

clue.text: Rock group might laugh

parts.note: thew means muscular strength, might
ho is a laugh

explanation.surface: A rock band that might find something funny.
explanation.definitionFit: The Who are a British rock band from the 1960s.

clue.text: It provides relief from cold, travelling around

parts.note: C is the abbreviation for cold, as on taps
a band on tour travels around

explanation.surface: Escaping the cold by travelling abroad.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Relief' is not respite but the relief of a landscape, as shown on a map.
explanation.definitionFit: Contour lines on maps show the height and shape of land, its relief.

clue.text: Greek island with hot club

parts.note: Cos (Kos) is a Greek island

explanation.surface: A sweltering Greek island with a nightclub.
explanation.definitionFit: A cosh is a short heavy club or bludgeon.

clue.text: Dashing fellow's got in bed for a smoke

indicators.note: got in means the next piece climbs inside the bed word

parts.note: a cot is a bed
a hero is a dashing fellow

explanation.surface: A dashing man has climbed into bed for a cigarette.
explanation.definitionFit: A cheroot is a cigar with both ends cut square, something to smoke.

clue.text: Two businesses showing growth, which will bear fruit

indicators.note: two means the piece is written twice

parts.note: CO is short for company, a business

explanation.surface: Two firms showing growth, which will pay off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Growth' and 'bear fruit' sound like business jargon; here they describe a plant.
explanation.definitionFit: The coco is the coconut palm, a tree that bears coconuts.

clue.text: On the radio, did rock'n'roll material

indicators.note: on the radio means as heard, giving the sound

parts.note: to rock and roll is to sway from side to side

explanation.surface: A broadcast about someone dancing to rock and roll in fabric.
explanation.walkthrough: Blue suede shoes are the rock'n'roll link that makes the surface hang together.
explanation.definitionFit: Suede is leather with a napped surface, used as a fabric.

clue.text: Protection against dripping tea, carrying one to drink

parts.note: a mac (mackintosh) is a raincoat

indicators.note: carrying means the tea word holds the next piece

parts.note: cha is tea
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A shield against tea spills while carrying a cup.
explanation.definitionFit: A macchiato is an espresso coffee marked with a little milk.
